data.text: **Middleware** extends Redux's capabilities by intercepting actions before they reach the reducer. It's the way to add custom logic like logging, crash reporting, API calls, and routing to your Redux application.

Middleware forms a **pipeline** around the dispatch function. When you dispatch an action, it flows through each middleware in order, giving each one a chance to inspect, modify, or stop the action before it reaches the reducer.

data.text: A Redux middleware is a curried function with three parameters: `store`, `next`, and `action`. This pattern allows middleware to access the store, pass control to the next middleware, or intercept actions.

data.title: Middleware Anatomy

rows: Log all actions and state changes

terms.definition: An ordered chain of middleware functions that each get a chance to process actions.
A function that passes the action to the next middleware in the pipeline.
A function that enhances the store itself, including middleware and other capabilities.
Any operation that reaches outside the pure function world: API calls, timers, DOM manipulation.

cards.title: Middleware
cards.content: Intercepts actions in the dispatch pipeline. Applied with applyMiddleware(). Best for cross-cutting concerns like logging and async operations.

cards.title: Store Enhancers
cards.content: Wraps the entire store creation. Can modify how store methods work at a deeper level. More powerful but rarely needed.

data.title: Logger Middleware
Middleware Order Matters
data.text: The order you list middleware in the array matters. For example, thunk should come before logger so async actions are resolved before logging.

data.title: Async-Aware Middleware
Build a Timing Middleware
data.description: Create a middleware that measures how long actions take to process and logs performance metrics. This is useful for identifying slow reducers.

items: Forgetting to call next(action) - action never reaches reducer
Forgetting to return the result of next(action)
Middleware order causing issues (e.g., logging before async resolves)
Creating new middleware instances on every render
Not handling edge cases like non-standard action shapes

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Middleware intercepts actions in the dispatch pipeline
Use applyMiddleware() to add middleware to the store
Great for logging, async operations, crash reporting, and analytics
data.takeaway: Middleware is the extensibility point in Redux that allows you to add cross-cutting concerns like logging, async handling, and error reporting.
